name: BimodalGaze
summary: Point with your eyes and, only if the gaze cursor is off, nudge it with a deliberate head movement; the switch to head control happens automatically.
howItWorks: The cursor follows gaze (Gaze Mode). Head movements that start within 150 ms of an eye movement and go in roughly the same direction (within 20°) are treated as natural support for the gaze shift and ignored; other head movements above 15°/s are treated as gestural and switch the cursor to head control (Head Mode) for refinement. A fast saccade (over 160°/s), or the cursor drifting more than 10° from gaze, returns it to Gaze Mode. Compared with Eye+Head Pinpointing (manual button switch) in VR (N=12, HTC Vive with Tobii, 3° targets at 10–40°, artificial gaze error added): all targets were reached and refinement was faster, but premature clicks in Gaze Mode made it about 140 ms slower overall; it beat Pinpointing on errors when eye tracking was least accurate. Selection was confirmed with a controller trackpad press in the study.

relationships.note: Automates Pinpointing's manual switch from gaze to head refinement.
